summary: Build advanced systems thinking skills to tackle complex problems with rigor and confidence. Learn practical models, tools, and interventions.
lede: Systems thinking for complex problems gives professionals a structured way to understand interdependencies, feedback loops, delays, and unintended consequences across an entire ecosystem. This five-day course helps you move beyond isolated symptoms by examining how policies, incentives, culture, technology, and external forces shape outcomes. You will practise causal loop and stock-and-flow diagramming, system archetype analysis, scenario modelling, and stakeholder synthesis. The course also introduces system dynamics, the Viable System Model, and Soft Systems Methodology so you can design system-aware interventions and translate insights into governance, OKRs, and portfolio decisions.
audienceIntro: This advanced systems thinking for complex problems training is built for senior professionals who already navigate complex initiatives and now need a more rigorous way to diagnose, design, and steer system-level change.
modules: Foundations of Systems Thinking for Complex Problems
Viable System Model for Organizational Design
Soft Systems Methodology and Multiple Perspectives
Systems Thinking in Governance, Risk, and Transformation
From Insight to Action: Designing Systemic Interventions
prerequisites: This is an advanced course intended for experienced professionals. You should have several years of responsibility for complex initiatives, programs, or multi-stakeholder change. Familiarity with basic problem-solving methods, causal reasoning, and using data or dashboards in decision-making is expected. No coding is required; system dynamics work uses visual modelling tools at an operational application level rather than technical engineering depth.
